message.content:
You are auditing output quality of a coding-agent CLI called "glint" (project at /home/lane/GR). The user's complaint: glint "can't manage to make a website with nice animations" — output is "incredibly stupid."

There are HTML files in /home/lane/GR that glint (or its lineage) produced or that serve as references: bring-back-fable5.html, embedme.html, fable-legends-index.html, and a site/ directory. Read ALL of them.

Your mission: produce a concrete, specific technical assessment of what makes these websites BAD — and what a great animated modern website would have that these lack. Be brutally specific, cite line numbers / exact code.

Cover:
1. Animation: is there any? CSS transitions/keyframes/scroll-triggered/JS animation libs? What's missing (easing, stagger, scroll-reveal, parallax, micro-interactions, page transitions)?
2. Layout & visual design: spacing system, typography scale, color palette, use of modern CSS (grid, clamp, custom props), responsiveness, dark mode.
3. Polish: shadows, gradients, glassmorphism, hover states, loading states, accessibility.
4. Code structure: inline vs external, use of any framework/CDN libs (GSAP, anime.js, Framer Motion, Tailwind), or all hand-rolled.

Deliver: (a) a ranked list of the top 8 concrete deficiencies with file:line evidence, (b) a short spec of what "AGI-level animated website" output should contain that's currently absent. Return findings as text — be dense and specific, no fluff.

content.text: Four files. Let me read all of them.
Interesting — `embedme.html` is actually quite sophisticated (SVG stroke-draw animation engine). Let me read the other two files.

I have all four files read in full. I have everything I need for a concrete, line-cited assessment. Here is my findings report. --- # Audit: glint-produced websites — animation & design quality ## Files reviewed - `/home/lane/GR/bring-back-fable5.html` (797 lines, hand-rolled dark dashboard) - `/home/lane/GR/fable-legends-index.html` (724 lines, hand-rolled marketing page) - `/home/lane/GR/site/index.html` (403 lines, the actual glint landing page) - `/home/lane/GR/embedme.html` (278 lines, a standalone SVG stroke-draw logo intro — the one genuinely good artifact) ## Headline finding The complaint is only half right. The **logo intro engine in `embedme.html`** (reused in `site/index.html` lines 71–313) is genuinely sophisticated: a runtime SVG path-splitter that clones each path into up to 2,600 dash-offset segments, staggers them outside-in, then fires a settle-pop, a screen-blend light sweep, and a per-letter 3D `rotateX` wordmark cascade with a gradient shimmer — all with a real `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback (`embedme.html:125–132`). That is above-average work. The problem is that **all the animation lives in that one bolted-on widget.** The moment the logo finishes drawing, every page becomes a static, scroll-dead document. The "stupid" verdict comes from the contrast: a flashy intro followed by zero motion, plus broken/fake mechanics. --- ## (a) Top 8 concrete deficiencies (ranked) **1. The "scroll animations" are fake — they animate on page load, not on scroll.** `fable-legends-index.html:526–533` declares `.fade-in{opacity:0; animation:fadeInUp ... forwards;}` with delay classes. That CSS animation runs immediately at load regardless of viewport position. The IntersectionObserver at `:700–710` then sets `entry.target.style.opacity = '1'` — but the element already animated to opacity 1 on load, and the observer never *triggers* the transform (it only sets opacity, which the keyframe already owns). Net effect: cards below the fold finish their entrance before the user ever scrolls to them. This is the single most "AI-slop" tell: animation code that looks right and does nothing. There is no `IntersectionObserver` at all in `bring-back-fable5.html` or `site/index.html`. **2. `site/index.html` — the flagship page — has literally zero entrance/scroll motion.** Everything after the logo is static. The only "animation" is `transition: all .2s` on buttons (`:28`) and `border-color .25s` on cards (`:47`). No section reveals, no staggered feature-card entrance across the 11 cards (`:362–372`), no animated terminal typing in the `.term` demo (`:332–352` is a static `
` block where a typewriter effect is the obvious win). The hero copy at `:315–322` just appears.

**3. No animation library anywhere — no GSAP, Framer Motion, anime.js, Lenis, ScrollTrigger, Tailwind.** All four files are hand-rolled `
